Baldur's Gate 2

This website has been created in order to help players - including myself, back when I played a lot more - to specifically play through the (old) game called Baldur's Gate 2 (= BG2). This game was originally released on the 21.09.2000 (21st of September, in 2000).

The main focus of this document here lies on playing through BG2 with useful mods installed. These mods may modify the game experience - and in most cases, enhance that experience as well. An initial play-through the original (or enhanced) BG2 game, will be referred to as a vanilla run.

Take note that this document may contain quite many spoilers, so it is recommended to only read it (and thus continue past this point) if you are ok with that or may need a bit of help when stuck in a (herein listed) mod.

After a player has managed to play through the original Baldur's Gate 2, that player may wish to change some parts of the game, via various tweaks or additional encounters. In other words: for many such players, the BG2 series can be enhanced via mods on subsequent play-throughs.

This document here yields useful information pertaining to these objectives. It will cover several different mods for Baldur's Gate 2, as well, although not necessarily in equal level of detail. In other words: some mods are tested more than others. Other mods are barely mentioned here at all.

Installation Order of BG2 Mods

The installation order of the mods in BG2 may be important, as some mods will only work if installed in the correct installation order.

For instance, NPC-related mods should typically go after quest-mods, simply because some NPCs will detect modded quest content and provide (more) interactions with these. You may find a mod NPC commenting on a certain mod quest, but only if the NPC can logicall follow the quest in the correct installation order.

Tweak mods, such as the legendary Tweaks Anthology, should always come last or close to the end of an installation list, as should mods that add new worldmap areas.

I keep track of my installation order in the file called array_mod_installation_order.yml. You can see the latest version of it either in the project (gem) called games, or on github here:

https://github.com/rubyFeedback/Baldurs_Gate_Data_Collection/blob/main/array_mod_installation_order.yml

In the past I also used to gather specific recommendations when the installation of a mod may fail or run into issues. For instance, the rather old NPC Strongholds mod can most likely be skipped, as the tweaks-mod allows you to play through stronghold mods, even without class restriction. When I typically play through BG2, I use the tweaks mod to enable playing through all stronghold mods. In this regard, the tweaks mod is, in my opinion, better than the old NPC Strongholds mod.

Since as of October 2026, though, as I was preparing to clean up the document here and bring it up to date, I decided that mentioning problematic mods may be outside the scope of this document. And some of these mods were improved, so old statements I made became outdated. Thus, this subsection here is quite short now, as I will no longer discuss bad mods specifically here.

Inns, Pubs and Taverns in BGII

The Mithrest Inn is an inn that can be found in Athkatla's Waukeen's Promenade.

Find the Nether Scroll for Edwin

This quest is triggered by travelling with Edwin to Athkatla's Graveyard District.

Use of the three entrances leading to the lower tombs, enter from the pyramid in southwest part of the map, make your way through heaps of undeads and spiders then into the lower dungeons from south, the nether scroll is obtained from Nevaziah, who did become a lich and can be found near his tomb, in the eastern area.

Five days afterwards, Edwin deciphers a part of the scroll and will receive a permanent -1 bonus to all saving throws, 50,000 XP and +20 to his lore.

A couple of days later, another decipher-step of the scroll transforms Edwin into a woman without being able to turn back. From this point on, some companions may have a rather interesting conversation with Edwina.

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Find_the_Nether_Scroll_for_Edwin

Class requirements in BG2

Cleric: Wisdom
Druid: Wisdom, Charisma
Fighter: Strength
Mage: Intelligence
Ranger: Strength, Dexterity, Wisdom
Thief: Dexterity

Efficient play-throughs with mods installed:

In the past this subsection focused on giving some advice in how to do an efficient run-through, including many mods, based on (primarily) power, but also on speed and efficiency.

When this document was updated in October 2026, the focus of this subsection changed slightly. Rather than making it as a step-by-step advice, this paragraph only contains a few helpful hints here and there.

In the first dungeon of BG2, make sure to obtain the Helm of Balduran as well as the Girdle of Bluntness. Alternatively you could install the mod Skip Chateau Irenicus (see here); the items can be found nearby to the starting position, after the first dungeon was skipped.

If you installed Lava's Southern District mod then it is recommended to visit it as soon as possible, and start to solve the various small quests there; in particular the crazy bard may have some items that can be useful, such as for a berserker/mage (the katana). Either way, doing so should yield some useful items and money early on. Consider purchasing at the least one Bag of Holding as well - some mods add them, such as the Mystigan merchant in the Government district.

In the vanilla variant of BG2, resting in the graveyard district does not cost anything, and it is easy to reach. No guards will wake up the party - though roleplay wise it may be questionable to sleep next to the dead, for some characters. If you installed the Jazon mod then you can find his heart in one of the tombs. Jazon is a very useful companion that may simplify some battles; at the least in that he may buy some time for others in the party to cause more damage.

Consider obtaining the Daystar sword from the lich in the Gate district. You can pick the lock and open the chest, then run out, sleep and return to kill the lich via Daystar. In fact, it may be possible to make short work of most liches with Daystar; Korgan was particular useful here for this task.

In one quest Boo is kidnapped - quite literally snatched away from Minsc. If Boo is recovered and the final riddle not solved completely, then a small figurine will be given to the party for finding Boo (and solving two of the three riddles).

Obtain the respite from Hexxat early on.

Steal the djinni flask in Trademeet, via Hexxat or another character. Alternatively, if you are about to finish the subquest from the djinni, you could kill the djinni outside the tent, rush in and initiate dialogue with the leader of the djinni. This will solve the quest and may be an option for parties not having a thief character at that point in time.

Obtain the Horn of Valhalla, to be found in the Bridge district. This horn can be upgraded twice in total.

Obtain the golem early on, to summon it quickly.

Obtain the moon dog figurine if a ranger.

Buy the mauler club for strength 18. Aerie may benefit from it, but also Viconia may benefit from it in the early play-time. (Viconia can boost her strength via a miracle, so the club may not be that useful in later stages of the game.)

Obtain the spider figurine item from the graveyard, from Paina. The party will also find a summon spider spawn scroll there.

Progress with Dusk's NPC mod (Autumn Fall), in particular to obtain the 100.000 gold coins as reward. This should then make it significantly easier to purchase some high-quality gear, such as the robe of Vecna.

Can wands be recharged in BG2?

You may be able to recharge a wand indirectly, if you sell them to a shopkeeper, then re-buy them. I have not tested this though.

There is also at the least one mod that allows the player to re-charge wands; a NPC can be found for this, in the Promenade District.

Nalia's main quest

As part of Nalia's main quest, Lord Farthington Roenall will come to the Keep, asking to speak to the player.

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Ruling_the_de%27Arnise_Keep_and_Lands

If the player refuses to see him, then one of his guards will enter and make a threat to Gorion's Ward, trying to intimidate them into giving up the Keep, before leaving.

If the player sees him, again, Lord Roenall demands that the player give the De'Arnise Keep to him. The player may either acquiesce, losing their Stronghold permanently, or throw him out (continues the Stronghold storyline).

Jan Jansen

Jan's home ("Jansen Stead") can be found in the Athkatla "Slums", but he is actually (initially) in the Government District, near the middle part of it, selling products without permission.

For his quest the party first has to talk to Lady Jysstev in the Government District (3300 exp), then talk to the owner of the Sea's Bounty Tavern, in the "Docks" district.

Jan has the Flasher master crossbow. He has an icon showing under his special abilities that allows him to make X new flasher masters per day. This may only work once you are out of ammunition, which allows Jan to conjure up some Bruiser Mates.

Anomen's quest relates primarily to his sister's death. After her death, Anomen will return home and become lawful good if he qualifies as a knight.

His quest will proceed as follows:

After Anomen has been in the party for five days, a servant of the Delryn family named Terl will appear and tell Anomen his sister Moira Delryn has been murdered.

Dragomir's tomb - Hexxat's first quest

To defeat Dragomir, +2 weapons are necessary.

Debuffing Dragomir is possible via „slow“ is also useful.

The main tank of the party, soaking up Dragomir's hits, should be kept alive. Also, consider using mirror image on the main tank as well as stoneskin before the beginning of the fight.

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Dragomir%27s_Tomb

The Claw of the Black Leopard (Hexxat's second quest):

Loot the sarcophagi for a Periapt of Life Protection and subsequently disarm traps as you venture forth, with the key. Then open the door at (x=1900, y=1600).

Open any sarcophagi nearby to awake five angry Greater Mummies to deal with, the middle sarcophagi (x=2100, y=1420) contains The Jade Fang dagger. If Keno died, more ghosts will attack the party from all sides along the way.

Take the east way to find Ki Chin Sang (x=1900, y=820) who holds the Key of the Master's Crypt. You can fight him for it. He will also hand it over voluntarily if you challenge the master's six 'most trusted lieutenants' in the hallway to the south. Accept the challenge for more xp: after you kill Borok-Tosst, Yi Niu, Weimin Min, Ming-hua Dai, Yi Kwon, and Jiang Dai who merge after clicking one of their sarcophagi, Ki Chin Sang will walk to you and hand over the key.

Alternatively, the key can be pickpocketed (confirmed with Jan @ 125 skill). Your first try will get a few coins.

Use the key to open the doors at (x=1350, y=550), disarm two traps to meet Nan Kung Chi at (x=2169, y=556), whatever you say will end up into a fight, loot his tomb at (x=2047, y=486). Once you possess the Claw of the Black Leopard, Hexxat will offer to be back to Amn, if you decide to stay a little longer (probably kill some ghosts for xp), just to tell her to wait then manual talk to her again.

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Hexxat%27s_request

Hexxat's third quest (The Tomb of the Prophet Unproved):

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Hexxat
https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Hexxat%27s_request

The Montaron quest as part of SoA

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Find_out_What_Happened_to_Montaron

Xzar, a companion from Baldur's Gate will approach the party and ask you to free Montaron, his fellow companion, from the Harpers.

Rylock, the doorman in front of the Harper building, is in the southwestern part of the "docks" district. He will ask the party to kill some evil creatures in Prebek's house before he will allow you to enter the building.

Thus, enter Prebek's House near the center of the area and defeat Prebek, Sanasha, and the goblins. Return to Rylock and then you can enter the building whenever you like.

When you are inside, the Harpers will say that you can't enter the floor above without harm if you don't have a Harper Amulet. An amulet can be found in one of the rooms on the base floors.

Go to the first level floor. With the Harper Amulet equiped, the Spectral Harpists won't attack you and your party and they will answer some of your questions as well. You will find some letters somewhere here which suggest that the Harpers have polymorphed Montaron into a bird.

Go to the room with the aviary. Enter the aviary and take the "Harper Bird" who was once Montaron.

Leave the harper building and give the bird to Xzar. He will cast a reverse polymorph spell, but the bird is actually an assassin from the Harpers named Lucette who kills Xzar (you can kill Xzar if you are quick enough for 4500xp). The party has been misled.

Kill Lucette for some additional experience. It requires a fast casting Slow or a well set-up thief with a backstab as she's out of sight quite quickly. She will appear behind Xzar and you may not see her if you're not directly facing him. (However had, this may mess up the quest.)

If you have Jaheira in your group, the "Summoned to the Harper Hold" quest will give you access again to the Harper Hold.

Searching the chests upstairs will reveal his body for an additional 20,000 experience (even if you previously opened and emptied all of them).

Being captured by Mind Flayers southeast of the drow city

It can be quite a challenge for some parties to defeat the mind flayers southeast of the drow city in BG2.

Should you have problems here, consider any of the following strategies - aside, of course, from being as high in level as possible before trying to fight the Mind Flayers.

- Chaotic command, a druid spell, can render the main actor invincible against Mind Flayers.

- Make use of the Illithid Serum on one of the machines in the southeast corner of the area, in order to free the slaves.

- Click on the large machine in the northeast corner of the room four times to obtain Control Circlets, four in total. If you should run out of Control Circlets, you can also transform into the Slayer to open the doors, as the Slayer is an immortal being.

- Once you have the elder brain blood, after killing the big master brain, go to the exit at the northeastern part of the map (same as the entrance, quite logically).

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Captured_by_Mind_Flayers

Combat strategies in general, with regards to BG2

Combat strategies that may work against a demilich, in a vanilla run:

→ use Melf's Minute Meteors
→ use a scroll of protection from undead
→ use spell immunity and choose abjuration

Note that the freedom spell can reverse imprisonment. For this to work it has to be cast in the area where the imprisonment happened. The scroll for Freedom can be obtained from the Arcana Archives. If the tweaks mod is used then it can also be purchased from Ribald.

Spell Immunity: Abjuration should also help against imprisonment. The ring of spell turning can also be used here. Shield of the Archons and Cloak of Atonement might help as well.

Deck of Many Things - DoMT (and Aesgareth)

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Aesgareth
https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Deck_of_Many_Things

Aesgareth (to be found as part of the Watcher's Keep) can simply be killed - the Deck of Many Things will be in his corpse, so you do not have to gamble if you merely wish to obtain the deck as such.

If you decide to gamble then it seems prudent to first gamble for the Spectral Brand. If you get cursed by "Strength", then you need to use "remove curse", a level 3 spell.

The Star card increases your "main stat" by 1. For single-class characters, this is obvious. For duals, I think it is the active class, and for multis, I have not yet found a correct guide. A fighter/thief will receive a dexterity increase. If you are unlucky, you can get a permanent save penalty from the Deck as well.

First draw:

bad: DONJON, EURYALE and RUIN
good: FLAMES, GEM and JESTER (+50.000 XP)

Lazarus' Missing Spellbook (in the Throne of Bhaal campaign)

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Lazarus%27_Missing_Spellbook

- After talking to Lazarus, speak to "Squip" just north of the Arcana Archives. He will tell the party that Hectan paid him to steal the book.

- Next, the party should venture to the "Tankard Tree inn" and speak to Hectan. He will admit to taking the book but will only give it back if Lazarus gives him a teleportation scroll to get out of the town.

- Go back to the Arcana Archives and speak to Lazarus. Tell him what Hectan wants in return for the book. Lazarus gladly gives you a teleportation scroll but also warns you that Yaga-Shura's mages have raised a magical barrier around the city. If Hectan tries to use the scroll, he will be killed.

- Go back to the Tankard Tree give the scroll to Hectan in return for the spellbook. If you don't warn him, he uses the scroll and gets blown up, and the party loses a reputation point.

- Return to Lazarus and give him the spellbook. All party members receive 5000xp and Lazarus will allow you access to his stock.

The Illithid Hideout in the Sewers of Athkatla

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Illithid_Hideout_in_the_Sewers

To open the secret door you need Sewer Key from Tazok in the "Domain of the Dragon"; his corpse contains that key. The Illithid Correspondence can be found there as well, but it is not a quest item. The Hammer of Thunderbolts can be found in this hideout.

Free the captive druids

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Helping_Irenicus%27s_captive_dryads

The party must venture to the "Windspear Hills" after having obtained the acorns from the first dungeon in SoA.

Once the party has arrived on the Windspear Hills, go to the southeast corner of the map there, where the Fairy Queen Vaelasa will be found.

Give her the acorns and the Dryads in the dungeon will finally be freed. The party will receive 32,500 XP upon handing the acorns over and a further 9,750 XP upon the Dryads' arrival, for a total of 42,250 XP.

Jon Irenicus

How can Jon Irenicus be defeated in a vanilla run, in the area before ToB begins, when Jon transforms into the Slayer?

You may be able to run away from Jon and his minions. The demons may follow the party while Irenicus stays put - and behind. First, kill all the demons, heal and buff your party as well. Then it should be easier to fight Irenicus, without being attacked by the demons.

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Jon_Irenicus
https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Baldur%27s_Gate_II_Chapter_7

Baron Ployer: saving Jaheira from the plague

https://baldursgate2.fandom.com/wiki/Save_Jaheira_from_Baron_Ployer%27s_Curse

- When you enter the "Sea Bounty" by the Docks, Baron Ployer, a former slaver, will confront Jaheira (if she is in the party that is). Three mages will appear and cast a curse on Jaheira.

- Next, enter the government building in the Government District and ask "Corneil" about Baron Ployer or the mages. He will not be very helpful.

- Resuming therein, speak to Terrece, who will be standing just outside the government building. He will offer to stay out of the coming fight for 1000 gold. For 2000 gold he will agree to kill Ployer.

- Enter Baron Ployer's home in the northeast side of the "slums" area, called the "Derelict Home". If you paid Terrece 2000 gold to kill Ployer, he will appear and do the deed. If you paid him 1000 gold to stay out of it, you can either kill Ployer by himself, or you can force him to remove Jaheira's curse. Jaheira will not honor the deal, however, and will kill Ployer. If Terrece was not bribed then the party will have to fight Baron Ployer and his three hired mages.

- Take the Lock of Jaheira's hair from Ployer's body and Jaheira will feel better. The curse will disappear after 24 hours.

Available Strongholds in Baldur's Gate II:

It is possible for an evil protagonist to acquire the Five Flagons Theatre as a stronghold without being a bard. More details can be found on the page Running the Five Flagons Playhouse.

Alternatively one could use the tweaks-mod and enable NPC strongholds without class-restrictions.

Thief stronghold:

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Thieves%27_Guild_Stronghold

How to cure the status "level drained" in BG2?

- In a temple, you can purchase the "restoration spell".

- Alternatively have a cleric cast "lesser restoration", a level 4 spell.

Personally I tend to prefer using Viconia here (when she is in the party; Aerie would do just fine too), casting lesser restoration in the process - this is both cheaper and saves some time than going to a temple usually.

The Bard class and their songs

The signature ability of the bard is their powerful battle song. While actively engaged in singing, the party will be fortified against fear, both natural and magical.

Most Bard songs work within a limited range, roughly fireball-sized. In the EE version 2.0+ there is also a +3 Luck bonus, as effect of the song.

The child Wellyn quest - a subquest of SoA

On the graveyard of Athkatla one can meet the ghost of Wellyn. He is missing his teddy bear.

Llynis - who stole the teddy bear - has a room at the "Copper Coronet", in the "Athkatla Slums" district.

Go confront Llynis and ask for the teddy bear. Depending on the dialogue options chosen, Llynis will either attack the party, or hand over the bear peacefully. Either way, you might as well loot his room when Llynis is gone.

Now return to the graveyard in the evening or at night and speak to Wellyn again. He will be so happy and will finally be able to rest in peace. The party receives 15,500 XP as reward.

Return to Wellyn's grave in the morning and speak to his parents, who are usually mourning nearby. His parents will be overjoyed that their little boy can finally sleep peacefully. The party will get an additional 5,000 XP.

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Put_the_Spirit_of_the_Child_Wellyn_to_Rest

Deirex's Tower (in the drow city)

Deirex's Tower is a two-story tower located in Ust Natha and is the home of Deirex the Lich. You must enter the tower if you want to retrieve the Jae'llat Wardstone from Deirex. Deirex will drop Lich's Tooth, which will allow access to Deirex's Cave, via the stairs on the outside of the tower.

Now head down to Deirex's Tower, Deirex the Lich is right there, and you are soon teleported to Jarlaxle's Pocket Dimension. The resident tells you that he wants the gem Deirex processes, he gives you one day to accomplish this before teleporting you back to Deirex's Tower.

Fight with Deirex, who is capable of casting Time Stop, Abi-Dalzim's Horrid Wilting and puts up as a normal lich battle (22,000 XP). Be sure to search his body for the Lich's Tooth and the Jae'llat Wardstone. Also search this place for treasures (some of which are trapped):

- Glitterdust scroll, Wizard Eye scroll, Deafness scroll, Contagion scroll, Remove Magic scroll, Limited Wish scroll and more.
- Leather Armor of the Viper +5
- Jarlaxle's Gems

Taking Jarlaxle's Gems will instantly teleport you back to the pocket dimension. Jarlaxle takes the Gems. Accept his thanks (2,500 Gold Piece or kill him (14,000 XP + 12,000 XP). In any case you will be teleported back to the tower.

The Tweaks Anthology mod

The latest version of the Tweaks Anthology mod is: 18

The Tweaks Anthology mod is a compilation of fixes, cosmetic changes, and tweaks that will run on every Infinity Engine game.

Each component of this mod can be installed separately, so the player can pick and choose only which ones they wish to install.

The mod will add Bags of Holding to Ribald. Such containers can also be made bottom-less, as part of this mod, which is quite convenient.

The tweaks mod can also add Universal Clubs, which allows mages to wield clubs and gain a proficiency point in clubs.

Not all tweaks are necessarily great, though - for instance, the Use BG Walking Speeds should probably not be used, whereas the Speed up de'Arnise Keep Stronghold Quest might be useful on subsequent play-throughs and could be enabled.

The mod can also extend the experience point caps, via Change Experience Point Cap. This one is quite useful.

The mod can be downloaded from the following location:

https://github.com/Gibberlings3/Tweaks-Anthology

Visit the homepage at:

https://github.com/Gibberlings3/Tweaks-Anthology

Trials of the Luremaster mod

The Trials of the Luremaster quest begins by talking to the halfling called Hobart Stubbletoes, who can be found either in the Umar Hills Inn (SoA), Amkethran Inn (ToB) or in the southeastern area of the Coalition Camp (SoD).

In the course of the adventure you have the opportunity to explore a haunted castle, test your mettle in challenging combat and lift an ancient curse. In addition to the original adventure, the mod provides various story and combat improvements as well as interactions from all of the Bioware and Beamdog NPCs. Some interesting items may also be purchased from the halfling.

The Luremaster will give at the least one riddle. The correct answer to that riddle is Wind.

In the large crypt, the party may eventually find four coffins. Place the four gathered Tales into the following coffins:

Western coffin: Tale of Sir Erris # two-handed axe +2
Southern coffin: Tale of Sir Giles # mace +1
Eastern coffin: Tale of Sir Zierkki # spear +1
Last coffin: Tale of Sir Geddian

For the larger area underneath you will need various gems and pearls that can be found in different chests, in particular:

(1) Flawed Moonbar Gem # can be found at the Dire Bears Area
(2) Flawed Skydrop Gem # found in the Minotaur Area
(3) Flawed Pearl # can be found in the Harpy Area, aka "Cave of the Stones"
(4) Flawed Emerald # can be found in the Spider Area
(5) Flawed Fire Agate Gem # can be found in the Jackal Area

These must then be converted into flawless gems, before they can be placed in the large circle containing the five slots. This step can be done in the Chest of Seasons, which is at the path in the southwestern area, at x: 730, y: 1470, within the Minotaur Area. The converted gems can then be found in each of the five altars.

Once the flawless gems have been obtained, they have to be put into the correct slot. "Heaven above" refers to the Star Sapphire. South to this the Flawless Waterstar Gem has to be put.

After defeating the Luremaster, a ring can be found, which has to be equipped and then used, in order to escape from the haunted castle.

Discussion about the mod can be found here:

The Tower of Deception

The Tower of Deception is a rather difficult side quest, unless properly prepared for it.

To defeat the (snake-like looking) Guardian protecting the Astral Shard, make sure that it does not have Stoneskin or Protection from Magical weapons active. Alternatively - or in addition to that - Ruby Ray of Reversal and Lower Resistance spells could be used against that Guardian, plus spell sequencer or the Greater Malison spell. Even then magic missile will do the trick.

In order to then defeat the Astral Shard, guarded by the Guardian, one can use a fireball or one of those exploding potions to damage it. A single exploding potion should suffice. Alternatively you can pick up fireball scrolls in the tower.

A7-GolemConstruction


The A7-GolemConstruction mod adds various golem building manuals.

The available golems will be:

Flesh Golems in lesser, regular, greater and perfect variants.
Clay Golems in lesser, regular, greater and perfect variants.
Stone Golems in lesser, regular, greater and perfect variants.
Iron Golems in lesser, regular, greater and perfect variants.
Mithral Golems in lesser, regular, greater and perfect variants.
Adamantite Golems in lesser, regular, greater and perfect variants.

In Shadows of Amn the Planar Sphere and Jermien's Home in Imnesville are suitable places for building golems.

The Wizard's Library on the second floor of Watcher's Keep can be used as well.

In order to construct a Perfect Flesh Golem, the Deep Bloodstone Gem is required. A regular bloodstone gem can be found in, for instance, Valygar's Home.

In order to construct a Perfect Clay Golem, four blocks of clay, one scroll of Haste and one bag of Enchanted Coral Powder are necessary. Without the enchanted coral powder one can only build a Greater Clay Golem.

Adamantite Golems require adamantine, as well as a thief with the "Use Any Item" ability.

These golems regenerate hitpoints per turn, and are immune to non-magical, +1 and +2 weapons.

Furthermore they can cast the "Trample" ability on enemies of normal size or smaller, which does 8d10+30 crushing damage and will also stun the target for one round (save vs. death at -4 penalty for half damage and avoid stun).

The Greater Adamantite Golem requires eight bars of adamantine. Its attributes are:

STR: 24
HP: 110
AC: 0
THAC0: 0
APR: 3/2
Saves: 1/3/2/2/4

The Perfect Adamantite Golem requires one drop of blood from a Solar or Fallen Solar.

Region of Terror mod

The Region of Terror mod is a mod about Drizzt do Urden.

Drizzt can be found on the second level of the very first dungeoon.

The mod also adds the city Arlax. There are three sewer entrances in Arlax; one is situated right after the main northern gate.

Furthermore, the mod contains a component where the party has to travel to Gaidan's Castle.

The village of Westchar is added by this mod. The house in the southeastern part of the village can be opened by a key given by the drow Alora, which can be found in Umar hills near the cave - but first you have to find Regis. The house in Westchar then allows the party to travel to the Realm of the Gragha.

Regis can be found in Montezuma's cave. Once he is freed he will give the next clue for the main quest, which is to visit the Umar Hills. Both Drizzt and the main character have to be close to Regis, in order for Regis to begin to talk.

One side quest of this mod makes use of Randall, a lethargic mage. five days after Randall has joined the party, when the protagonist has more than 250.000 XP, a mage labeled 'Necromancer' approaches the party while traveling outdoors. Razor can not be defeated; instead, when his hit points are reduced to 1, he will initiate a new dialog and reveals that he and his accomplice Marcus murdered Randall's real father. But before Razor can narrate the whole story, he perishes.

The Quest for the Eye of a God can be started by having Pip forge an item, by making use of a Rock of a Glowing Star. This can be done by, for instance, giving Pip a chain mail armor.

In one city a demi-lich can be found. Killing him will yield a mithril chainmail (which would be quite useful for Drizzt), and a tooth of the demilich, granting immunity against normal weapons.

Solution for the Test of Intelligence:

3,2,2,4,5

Brynnlaw

Shadows of Amn chapter 4 brings the party to Brynnlaw. Here Brother Martin has to be found outdoors near the Pirate Lord's Home, and when you are ready, ask him to teleport you to Spirit Soaring.

This quest has to be solved in this chapter, in order to complete the Region of Terror mod.

City of the Gragha

The answer to the riddle, as text, is kind of the order that is shown, as-is. So simply type "1" to select the first answer - this should suffice for all subsequent answers.

Bremen

A walkthrough for Bremen can be read here:

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Region_of_Terror_walkthrough/Bremen

The Ice Temple can be found as part of Bremen - see the next subsection.

Ice Temple

In order to open the talking door, the "Mysterious Scroll" from the hermit is required.

If instead you wish to solve the monk's riddle, you must place the gems in the following order, from bottom left:

yellow, violet, dark red, light red, dark green, light blue (= sapphire), light green, dark blue, black, white.

Abbot Baurmin can be found on the second level, in the most southern room (called Sanctuary room).

https://baldursgate.fandom.com/wiki/Region_of_Terror_walkthrough/Ice_Temple

Eye of a God Cave

To start The Quest for the Eye of a God, talk to Pip Grayfoot and let him forge something using a Rock of a Glowing Star.

This causes Pip to "graduate" from his apprenticeship, and set up his own smithy nearby.

Next, talk to Pip at his new smithy, and ask him if there are other forging gems beside the ones in his recipe book. He tells you about a legendary gem called "The Eye of A God", and marks a cave near Athkatla on your worldmap.

Four tablets have to be gathered on the first level. Once they have been collected they should be shown to the guardian, who resides at the bottom-left area.

Inside the cave, Lord Garrax can be found. How to defeat him?

- Have a Wish prepared.
- Be wary of the spellcasters, for they can gate in new demons.
- Killing the summons is useful, as they do not replenish eventually.

Tales of the Deep Garden

Tales of the Deep Garden can be started by talking to the crazy mage (the Mysterious Wizard) in the Government district of Athkatla, in the large, central park area there.

To participate in the tournament, a small riddle has to be solved first - the correct answer is Mermaid. Then, four items have to be found within three days.

(1) The first item can be found in the slum-district, at the southwestern corner of the tavern - look for a beggar. After asking for a coin he will attack the party.

The third item can be obtained in the Temple district, in the southwestern part, from a NPC.

The fourth item can be found in the Flagron Inn, at the bar, where Barney, a fat man stands.

Now you have to collect several colours, in order to solve the main quest.

(1) Violet can be found on the table in the south-western part of the map.
(2) Gold and Silver can be found in the first cave, in the southwestern part of the map.
(3) Green can be taken from the tree in the second cave; that tree can be found in the southeastern part of the map. Blue can be simply taken from the well in the northwestern part, also in the second cave.
(4) Once the party has the Blue colour, they can visit the House of Gray. Inside of it is an old man called Senex. He wants to see the Blue colour and will give the Gray colour.
(5) Red can be found in the pit in the southeastern area. Here the party has to take Red from the corpse and additionally take a dried plant from the hiding place, needed for the Green Witch.

(6) The black colour can only be obtained after the party has gathered eight colours already.

Silvertongue (a woman) yields the following rewards, sorted by usefulness (top is best, bottom is worst), for a cost of 16.000 gold coins:

(1) - Green: -1 to spell casting time
(2) - Violet: regenerate 1 HP every 9 seconds
(3) - Silver: +15% to magic resistance
(4) - Red: +1 THAC0, +1 Damage
(5) - Yellow: +1 AC
(6) - Black: +5 saves against death, -1 reputation
(7) - Gray: +1 attack per round, -3 to death saves, -6 HP, -2 to THAC0
(8) - Gold: +10% resistance to acid, cold, electricity and fire
(9) - Amber: +7 to HP
(10) - Blue: +20000 experience points

The Riddle of the Hooded Man can be solved as follows:

2, 4, 7, 2

Dark Tidings

Dark Tidings begins in the Docks district of Athkatla. Here, at the Sea's Bounty Tavern, one has to go upstairs and talk to Thalass.

On the Lighthouse floor 4, the party can find a locked chest containing the cellar key, as well as a diary. So, head to the cellar next.

The wall stones have to be pushed in the following order:

Fire (left)
Water (bottom-right)
Earth (top-right)
Air (top-left)

Next, take the shadow brick and place into the ground container on the left side of the first room in the lighthouse. Then let one party member wear the cultist helmet from the third floor, which will reveal a secret door on the left wall. Pass this secret entrance, then click on the creepy shadow portal on the cave wall behind it.

Take the Luminous Crystal from the altar, to cause the Aspect of Tharizdun to appear.

After having defeated the Aspect of Tharizdun, complete the ritual. Go back to the very first floor of the lighthouse. Place the luminous crystal in the container at the base of the central altar. Proceed by casting the following three spells in the following order:

Protection From Evil
True Seeing # via a scroll
Dispel/Remove Magic

All of these spells must be cast inside the ritual chamber.

The latest version of the Dark Tidings mod is: 3.2

The White Queen mod

To start The White Queen storyline buy a new book at the book merchant's store on the Promenade.

There is also a small side quest, where the party has to collect wine.

The demon (in the house where the White Queen resides) offers a powerful sling. The other rewards would be 15.000 gp or 25.000 xp (or a change to Reaction), but the sling is definitely the item to go for here.

Call of the lost goddess

The Call of the lost goddess mod.

A new city district is added by this mod, called Goldspires.

This mod also includes over 40 new unique items.

After having removed fear from the Tree (use the Remove Fear spell), one can take the horn of the demon from the container near the Tree.
